title: Formal and informal words 2
subtitle: cops, quid, telly, nosh
summary: Recognise short informal words, clipped forms and slang, understand what they mean, and know when they are and are not appropriate.

lesson.heading: Monosyllabic informal words
lesson.text: Informal versions of words are often short and **monosyllabic** - they consist of one syllable. The neutral word is usually the longer one.

examples.text: His dad spent ten years in the **nick**.

lesson.note: Also: I always go by **tube** (the London Underground) and I'll get a **cab** from the station (a taxi).

lesson.heading: Clippings
lesson.text: Shortening a word - a **clipping** - tends to make it less formal, though these forms are acceptable in a wide range of contexts and some, like *fridge*, are now the usual word.

examples.text: We should put an **ad** / an **advert** in the **paper**.
Can I use your **mobile**? I need to **phone** my brother.

lesson.note: Also: There's milk in the **fridge** (refrigerator), and Would you like to be a **celeb** (celebrity, a famous person)?

lesson.heading: Slang
lesson.text: **Slang** is extremely informal language. It makes speech vivid and colourful, but it is easily used inappropriately. It is mainly spoken, though it also appears in the popular press and in novels. Slang changes fast, so some words go out of fashion - you may still meet them in films and books. Some slang can cause offence.

examples.text: People obsessed with computers or other equipment: **nerd**, **geek**, **anorak**
Jobs: **quack** (doctor), **shrink** (psychiatrist), **the old bill** (the police), **squaddie** (a soldier of low rank)

lesson.heading: Short forms ending in -y or -ie
lesson.text: Another way of making an informal word is to shorten it and add **-y** or **-ie**. These are very common in friendly conversation and almost never appropriate in writing.

examples.text: Let's have **brekkie** before we leave tomorrow.
It's a nice day. Let's have a **barbie** and eat in the garden.
D'you want a **biccy** with your coffee?
Jenny turned up at the party with her new **hubby**.
Oh, let me see your holiday **piccies**!

lesson.text: Keep slang in your passive vocabulary: understand it when you hear it, but think twice before using it yourself.

exercises.prompt: *JIM:* Annie, can you lend me ten ___? (informal)
exercises.explanation: Quid is the informal word for pounds; it has no plural -s.

exercises.prompt: *JIM:* My bicycle's not working, so I'll have to get a ___. (informal)
exercises.explanation: Cab is the informal word for a taxi.

exercises.prompt: *JIM:* The ___ at our flat is empty, as usual. (informal)
exercises.explanation: Fridge is the clipped form of refrigerator.
The tube is the informal name for the London Underground.

exercises.prompt: Match each slang word with its neutral equivalent.
He spent two years in the nick for stealing cars. A more formal word for *the nick* is ___.
exercises.explanation: The nick is informal for prison.

exercises.prompt: The cops arrived shortly after the accident. A more formal word for *cops* is ___.
exercises.explanation: Cops and the old bill are informal words for the police.

exercises.prompt: He's quite a celeb in the world of poetry. What is the full form of *celeb*?
exercises.explanation: Celeb is a clipping of celebrity - a famous person.

exercises.prompt: (formal email) I should like to enquire about the cost of ___ on your website.
exercises.explanation: Ad and advert are informal clippings of advertisement.

exercises.prompt: (exam essay) The Internet and ___ are probably the biggest influences on young people today.
exercises.explanation: Telly is too informal for an exam essay; use television.

exercises.prompt: (recipe in a cookery book) Next, slice the ___ and place them on top of the meat.
exercises.explanation: Spuds is the informal word for potatoes.

exercises.prompt: (exam essay) ___ face stiff competition these days from TV and internet news.
exercises.explanation: Paper is a clipping of newspaper.

exercises.prompt: (formal university publicity) The Faculty offers courses in ___ science.
exercises.explanation: Vet is a clipping of veterinary surgeon.

exercises.prompt: Match each -y / -ie word with what it means.
Sort each word into the right group.

exercises.statement: Slang is mainly used in speech, but it is also often found in the popular press and in literature.
exercises.explanation: Correct - and because slang changes quickly, older slang survives in novels and films.
